_note: Round 56 (more findable pages, owner: "use what we have and show it in a new manner ... split numbers that are together"): the generated page families, written by seo_pages.mjs with seo_families.mjs from the map's own numbers, in every site language. parts: one page per part of the panel (key) with its address (slug) and side (ua: support for Ukraine; back: money flowing back from it; rus: what Russia kept from trade; frozen: the return Russia lost on frozen money; cost: outside the totals). A part gets a page only where at least minCountries countries have it and the amounts add up to at least minTotal (EUR bn, by size), and not when a topic page of seo_topics.json already ranks it (rank: part:<key>). Its name in each language is in seo_i18n.mjs (PART). years: the years with a page of support for Ukraine (/ukraine-aid-<year>/) and of trade with Russia (/trade-with-russia-<year>/); the last year runs to the data's last month. compare: pairs of countries (ISO codes, in the order searched) with a page /compare/<a>-vs-<b>/, from the keyword research of 26 October 2026; pairwiseTop: the largest donors to Ukraine in euros, every pair of them compared too (the larger donor first).

country._note: Round 57: the rule of round 56 that gives an English country page the title "Does ... trade with Russia?" (seo_templates.mjs): where its trade with Russia is searched at least minTrade times (pipeline/seo_demand.json), at least ratio times more than its aid or help, and its aid is searched fewer than maxAid times (the countries whose aid is much searched keep the aid question). It replaces the list of ten countries with hand-written titles.

relations._note: Round 58: the country page's question on its relations with Russia, in the searchers' words ('Turkey Russia relations', 'Türkei Russland Beziehung', 'russia and south africa'), answered from its trade, support and net: in a language where the single-country queries of these clusters (seo_demand.json byLang) reach minDemand.

explain._note: Round 58: the explainers of seo_i18n.mjs EXPLAIN, shown where a topic page of seo_topics.json lists them (explain), and each also an FAQ entry (JSON-LD) in a language where the search demand of its keyword cluster (seo_demand.json _topics) reaches minDemand. An explainer without a cluster is never an FAQ entry.

armedItems._note: Round 58: the kinds of military supplies a country sent to Russia, in the searchers' words ('North Korea soldiers and shells', 'Iran drones'), named in titles, headings and questions only where the data have them: the country's weapons and troops sent to Russia come to at least minEur (EUR bn, full value) and src is one of the sources of its military_rus entry in data.json (the research that names those supplies). Their words in each language are in seo_i18n.mjs (S item).
